titleEn: When Thunder Rumbles, Into the Shed!

pages.text: "Roll along!" Pipo rolled a wooden ball on the hill. Sheep bounced after it. The sky slowly darkened. "I will play as much as I can until rain comes!"
Then rumble—the sky roared. Sheep pricked their ears and trotted toward the shed below. Pipo picked up the ball again. "A little more!" Raindrops began to fall.
Below the hill, quick-stepping Mr. Horse reached out. "Pipo, do not stay on the hill when thunder rumbles. Come down quickly, into the shed!" Hugging the ball, Pipo held his hand. "Yes, Mr. Horse!"
At the shed, Mom brought all the sheep inside and closed the door. "A sturdy shed is safest when thunder rumbles." Outside, rain was already pouring.

"Shall we be little lambs?" Mr. Horse whispered. "At a rumble, a lamb comes here first and buries itself in hay." Pipo slipped into the hay and called, "When thunder rumbles, into the shed!" Lambs huddled beside him.

Mom bent down and showed three fingers. "One, thunder means stop playing on the hill! Two, run into the shed! Three, when thunder stops, leave holding a grown-up's hand!" Pipo nodded. "I can do it like a lamb!"

Through a door gap, flash—the sky brightened, then darkened. In the hay, Pipo stayed close to Mr. Horse and watched the gap. He was not scared, with Mr. Horse and Mom there. In his heart he called, When thunder rumbles, into the shed!

Much later, thunder stopped. Rain stopped too. Mom held Pipo's hand and led him slowly outside. "Our Pipo was brave through the thunder!" Crouching by the door, hands at his chest, Pipo lifted his shoulders proudly.

Days later, another rumble! Pipo ran into the shed before the sheep. "One, thunder means stop playing! Two, into the shed! Three, when it stops, leave holding a grown-up's hand!" Sheep followed in a line.
That evening, Mom hugged Pipo tightly. "Even scared, you ran to the shed. Wonderful!" At thunder, a sturdy shed was a safe place. From her arms, he called, "When thunder rumbles, into the shed!"
